title: Membrane-bounded cells that swim and divide, from noise
route: An Allen-Cahn cell with a link ring (phase_membrane) plus a self-repellent trail (kstrail) or a Frey-type mobility switch; see Q:membrane-swimmer-divider.

title: Swimming, dividing, bounded cells from noise that a Laplacian-only twin cannot match
route: The ringed active-nematic rods (20261025T1141-c11-active-nematic-ringed) are the first SIBMD; run their matched passive twin (zeta=0, or the active stress replaced by linear diffusion at comparable rates) on the claim's seeds and have a reviewer check it with bd_supported.

title: Swimming, dividing cells whose wall holds their contents
route: Make a boundary do work: let the active-nematic rods' surfactant ring gate a cargo species across the interface (the ring is passive today), or give c03's gated FCH micelles (IBWD) a motility drive; W needs its wall-ablation control.

title: Containment that daughters inherit through division
route: A gated wall (min or harmonic face mobility) that holds a fast species through pinching: xcell-a's gate or ad7's shell on a dividing cell.

title: Heredity with selection driven only by intrinsic deaths
route: membrane_evo with the imposed death disks replaced by whole-body deaths from an extensive maintenance cost; see Q:autonomous-l7-identity-deaths. Claims must name this challenge.

title: Reproducing organized cells that a Laplacian-only twin cannot match
route: Run the owed matched Laplacian twins (Q:owed-laplacian-twins, Q:bd-ad7-gate-vs-lowered-d) on a dividing organized cell.

title: Organized dividing cells that live on a consumed, regrowing resource (not by construction)
route: Lenia with a conserved nutrient gated by the shell (Q:lenia-closed-nutrient-gated-shell), or r-two56 on food (Q:rtwo56-food-limited-cells), with a fork test.

title: Self-propelled organized individuals that repair
route: Damage a mature swimming cell (kstrail crescent with a wall, or an Allen-Cahn swimmer) with an undamaged twin.

title: Interacting populations that reproduce and eat
route: evopursuit prey-predator with fission and a food ledger; see Q:evopursuit-closed-ledger-l7.

title: New kinds keep appearing and replacing old ones
route: Requires autonomous heredity first; then long runs with a novelty measure that does not saturate.

title: A swim-before-divide minority spreads by selection where swimming pays
route: Start from the Marangoni rods (20261026T0505-c34-nematic-marangoni). There, 2-5% of dividing rods swim 3 of their own lengths between their own birth and their own division, and the trait is redrawn every cycle rather than inherited (20261026T1530-c00-marangoni-minority-lineages). Take the first of Q:marangoni-swim-screen, Q:marangoni-turnover-persistence, Q:marangoni-sink-escape, Q:marangoni-heritable-ladder and Q:marangoni-swimmer-spread that has no attempt, and announce and publish it under its own Q: task. A claim meets this challenge when all seven conditions hold on paired fresh seeds. (1) Heredity: the trait passes through fission in a species the bodies copy themselves. A surfactant kind with majority-feedback production counts; a label or parameter that a division rule hands to daughters does not. The trait varies only through a mutation operator that picks bodies by identity from an RNG seeded only by the run seed. Kind changes of living bodies outside mutation events stay below 1 per 10 mutation events, and merges are reported separately. (2) Turnover: in every arm, births continue for at least 3 generations after the population plateaus. They come from the environment's own dynamics or from trait-blind removal drawn the same way in every arm, and no rule reads a body's kind, speed, displacement or age. (3) Start: the ancestors are a single kind, and at most 20% of their dividing tracks pass. (4) Arms: the selective environment E; a control with the same supply process and turnover, in which moving cannot change survival or supply (for sink discs, remove the bodies inside each disc when it opens); and the identical-event twin in E, where every kind gets the ancestral value and the same mutation and removal draws. The twin absorbs drift, mutation bias and any direct effect of E on individuals. (5) Response: for each birth cohort, one median cycle wide, two quantities must rise more in E than in the control and more than in the twin: the share of split-born dividing tracks that pass PROTOCOL's M gate, and the pre-registered trait mean (for example the mean mar_k over living bodies). Each comparison needs a one-sided paired sign test with p < 0.05 (6 of 6 or 7 of 8 seeds). Pooled over seeds, the passing share in E's last third of cohorts must be at least twice the twin's. (6) Selection on the capability: in E, passers leave more descendants than non-passers of the same kind, counted two median cycles after their division (pooled, one-sided p < 0.05). (7) Self-propulsion: E with the drive off (mar=0) has no passers at equal counts, and each passer's rear tip advances at least 2/3 of its net displacement. Making the capability typical (half of a late cohort) is the follow-up challenge. Claims must name this challenge.
